A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RiboSphere study. All 15 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, inverse-folding, RNA–ligand binding and motif analyses, with additional reconstruction and sampling-temperature results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds inverse-folding structural-consistency scores and further reconstruction depth comparisons.

M1.justification: The encoder–FSQ–flow architecture, objectives and downstream procedures remain unchanged. The new FSQ appendix documents the existing quantizer. Its corrected description of the inverse-folding adapter feeding a GVP decoder agrees with v1 Section 3.5; the added depth configurations are experimental variants.

E1.justification: The RNA reconstruction and inverse-folding data, Robin and Biosensor datasets, and task coverage are retained. Refolding generated sequences adds evaluation of existing inverse-folding outputs without introducing a new dataset or population. Neither version reports multi-chain experiments.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes RiboPO, previously reported with diversity 0.89 and recovery 0.506. RiFold, RDesign, RIDiffusion and gRNAde remain, and Table 3 retains all binding comparators. EternaFold and RhoFold serve as evaluation tools.

E3.justification: Inverse-folding evaluation expands substantially from sequence recovery/diversity to EternaFold secondary-structure consistency using scMCC and RhoFold assessment using RMSD, TM-score and pLDDT. Tables 1 and 4 also extend tested encoder/decoder depth configurations, including two- and four-layer decoders. Existing dataset splits and temperature-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 extends the depth ablation with E4-D8, E6-D4 and E8-D2 configurations at dimension 256, 11 atoms and 240 tokens, strengthening the comparison of encoder/decoder depth allocation. Its E4-D6 row already appeared in v1 Table 5. Existing motif and temperature-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix C.2 retains sampling 16 sequences per structure. The added pLDDT column is a structure-prediction evaluation metric, not uncertainty estimation for the aggregate experimental comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds structural results: RiboSphere scores 0.63 scMCC, 11.54 RMSD, 0.29 TM-score and 0.55 pLDDT, leading scMCC but showing mixed 3D performance. Table 1 exchanges the 4,375-token A1/A11 results: RMSDs change from 1.35/1.25 to 1.25/1.35, with corresponding metric and utilization swaps. Three depth configurations gain results, and RiboPO entries disappear. Retained sequence and binding scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 explicitly formalizes FSQ rounding, the Cartesian-product codebook and its cardinality, and a mixed-radix token-index bijection beyond v1’s abbreviated equation. Other mathematical edits mainly correct notation and typesetting; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of SE(3)-invariant features with geometry-aware features learned using centering and rotation augmentation. The principal contribution bullets, headline reconstruction and recovery claims, and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits current training/evaluation to single-chain RNA and treats multi-chain modeling as future work. It softens augmentation-based symmetry assurances and removes the appendix’s physical-plausibility guarantee. Section 4.3 newly interprets scMCC as motif preservation and attributes lower pLDDT to predictor limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-repository access information in the abstract and Appendix B.3 details on FSQ rounding, token indexing and codebook-size construction. The adapter description is clarified. Optimizer, hardware, learning rate and training-duration disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Seven references are added for previously named baselines, including RiFold, RDesign, RIDiffusion and GraphDTA. Section 2.2 revises the claimed relationship to multi-chain research from addressing that gap to a possible future extension. The broader related-work discussion remains stable.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify symmetry, the adapter and inverse-folding findings. v2 adds an FSQ subsection and acknowledgements, corrects notation and author information, and updates publication front matter. The main section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains rows, Table 2 becomes a full-width table with structural-metric columns and an RNA-corrected caption, and Table 3 gains baseline citations. Figures are resized or relocated, and Table 5 moves within the appendix. The existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Structural-consistency evaluation and additional depth ablations strengthen empirical support, while FSQ details, code-access information and narrower symmetry/applicability claims improve clarity. These gains are limited by the unexplained removal of RiboPO and the retained atomic-granularity interpretation despite Table 1 now assigning the best reconstruction results to the single-atom model.
